thread:
maria (support): heads-up — enterprise customer acme-med reports one user can't open Project Settings > Members (Console shows 403). API calls with the same user API key return 200. customer says this started right after we completed the org-split last night :confused:

maria (support): screenshot: https://redwood-internal.s3/xxxx/acme-403.png — user email: joanne@acme-med.com, project id: proj_02a9, new org id: org_new_9f2

tom (eng-sre): thanks — can you paste the exact console error message (copy from the browser console) and the request id if available? also which org was the project previously under?

maria (support): console shows modal: "You don't have permission to view this (403)"; network request header contains x-request-id: rqd-20260315-11-7b9c; project belonged to org_old_1b7 before split. customer confirms project migrated to org_new_9f2 during the split job id job-2026-03-14-22

sre-bot: automated job notification: "org-split job-2026-03-14-22 completed; migrated 42 projects; migrated role-bindings: 0 (manual review required)"

kai (platform): that log from bot is the hint — looks like role-bindings didn't migrate for project-level collaborators. can you confirm whether joanne was a direct project collaborator or inherited via an org-level group?

maria (support): customer says she was a member via an org-wide Okta group (ACME-Dev-Team) that we mapped to an org-level role in the old org. they didn't have project-level direct invites.

tom (eng-sre): reproducing locally — when org_id in role_binding points to org_old_1b7 but project now lives under org_new_9f2, our console access check fails because we verify project->org mapping. API token scopes pass because token is scoped to the project id, but console uses the role-binding lookup path which is org-scoped.

kai (platform): workaround: add the user as a direct project collaborator (temporary) or add their Okta group to the new org's role mapping. immediate steps for CS: run:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/proj_02a9/members \  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"email":"joanne@acme-med.com","role":"project.viewer"}'```this grants console access instantly.

kai (platform): permanent fix (engineering): we need to migrate orphaned role_bindings pointing to the old org id. planned command (internal-only) — do not run without ops approval:
```
# list orphaned bindings
SELECT id FROM role_bindings WHERE org_id='org_old_1b7' AND project_id IS NOT NULL AND project_org_id='org_new_9f2';
# update to new org
UPDATE role_bindings SET org_id='org_new_9f2' WHERE id IN (<ids>);
```

kai (platform): i'll open an infra change with a safe rollback and audit trail, but we can do the direct collaborator workaround now.

liz (customer-success): pinging customer with the workaround now. telling them adding joanne as a direct member will restore console access immediately; we'll follow up once eng schedules the migration. :thumbsup:

maria (support): customer accepted the workaround and added joanne as project.member. confirmed they can view Members page now. i'll keep this thread open until eng runs the migration.

tom (eng-sre): logged an internal ticket INFRA-4981 to migrate role_bindings for org_old_1b7 -> org_new_9f2 and mark projects where migration didn't auto-run. assigned to kai for scheduling.

kai (platform): ETA for manual migration window: tomorrow 2pm PST, low-traffic window. will post runbook and expected downtime (none for console reads; writes to role_bindings will be safe).

maria (support): thanks all — closing customer-facing loop. will update after migration completes.

liz (customer-success): customer notes they'd like a short RCA once done. i'll collect the ask.

maria (support): noted. will attach job logs and list of patched role_binding ids in the RCA. :white_check_mark:
